messages:
Nina (Support): heads-up — AuroraMed trial can't finish onboarding; doc ingestion returns 422 during indexing. Many trial seats stuck.
Raj (Support): repro: POST /v1/docs -> 200 accepted -> async index -> 422 {"error":"index schema mismatch"} request req_a3d9c at ~09:02 ET across 3 regions.
Nina (Support): they're worried about next week's renewal check-in; escalating to CS for priority handling and comms.
Tara (CS): thanks. Quick asks: how many users impacted? sample payloads? PII risk?
Raj (Support): ~24 trial users, 6 org users. Payloads show nested arrays with nulls in patient.addresses. No unexpected PII surfaced. Samples on ticket https://app.redwood/tkt/8019.
Tara (CS): ops plan: 1) pause automatic retries for affected orgs; 2) offer CSV import as workaround; 3) propose a short pilot extension if needed. Drafting customer note.
Ravi (Engineering): root cause: recent validation tighten rejects nulls in nested arrays. Can relax validation and push patch in ~2 hours; transform pipeline would take longer.
Ben (AE): looping in Aurora contact Sara for consent and whether they prefer us to transform. Sara is privacy-sensitive, so ask explicitly.
Maya (CS Lead): legal might need to weigh in if we touch raw docs. Tara, include explicit consent ask in message. I'll stand by for credit escalations.
ops-bot: Support ticket updated SUP-8019 priority P1 assigned to eng-ml.
Nina (Support): paused retries for orgs aurora-trial-1..6 to avoid duplicate records.
Raj (Support): customer replied: they cannot re-export data today; asked us to handle transform.
Tara (CS): propose two options in message: (A) temporary validation relaxation (fast) or (B) CSV upload UI (manual). Recommend (A) + offer (B) later plus a 7-day trial extension and an enablement call.
Ravi (Engineering): I can cut a relaxation patch and run canary in ~90m; need test samples.
Ben (AE): scheduling 11:30 ET sync with Sara to walk through options; will include credit offer as gesture.
Maya (CS Lead): legal note: get explicit written consent for modifying data-in-flight; relaxing validation without retention is low risk but require customer OK. Created LEGAL-3344.
Tara (CS): draft to Aurora: "Hi Sara — sorry about the friction. We can relax our optional-field validation in ~2 hours to resume your trial flows, or enable a CSV upload. If you approve the validation change, please confirm that temporary processing (no additional data retention) is acceptable. We can also provide a 7-day extension and a 30-min enablement call."
Nina (Support): customer replied: "Approve (1) — do it now."
Ravi (Engineering): canary results: 18/20 processed; two failed due to legacy enums. Preparing prod push in 35m after smoke tests.
Raj (Support): dedupe TTL set to 12h to protect against re-index collisions.
Ravi (Engineering): prod patch deployed 11:45 ET, 26/26 queued trial docs processed successfully.
Tara (CS): sending post-fix note with offer: 7-day extension + enablement session tomorrow to review root cause and onboarding tips. Will capture feedback for product docs.
Maya (CS Lead): escalate any credit beyond 7 days to me and finance; add optional data-sanitization guidance to onboarding docs.
Nina (Support): closing P1 — will reopen if further failures.
Tara (CS): handoff summary for renewal playbook: support escalation -> validation regression -> retry pause -> customer-approved temporary validation relaxation -> prod patch -> enablement + 7-day extension offered -> action: update onboarding docs.
Maya (CS Lead): thanks team. Tara, please add this to the renewal notes so AE has context for next week's touch.
